Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The diagram shows two production possibility curves for an economy. services N L M K O goods Which combination of movements correctly illustrates these changes in production? short-run long-run no economic growth economic growth economic growth

options.B: K to L M to N L to M
options.C: M to N K to L L to M

questions.questionText: What distinguishes the very long run from the long run?

options.A: the ability to change resource allocation
options.B: the ability to change the state of technology
options.C: the absence of government market intervention
options.D: the existence of variable factors of production

questions.questionText: Which statement is a positive statement?

options.A: The distribution of income and wealth in most western European countries is unequal.
options.B: The government ought to increase income tax on high earners.
options.C: There should be more legal rights given to workers to protect their status in the workplace.
options.D: Wages of those on low incomes should be increased.

questions.questionText: What could not cause a shift in an individual’s demand curve for good Z?

options.A: a change in advertising expenditure on Z
options.B: a change in the individual’s income
options.C: a change in the individual’s tastes
options.D: a change in the price of Z

Which example of consumer behaviour would create consumer surplus?

options.A: when a consumer does not spend all of her income each month
options.B: when a consumer pays less than they are willing to pay for a good
options.C: when a consumer throws away vegetables because they bought too much
options.D: when a good is purchased in order to resell it at a higher price

questions.questionText: A manufacturer reduces the price of its goods after developing a more efficient manufacturing process. It makes leather belts that compete against belts made of artificial material. What are the likely outcomes of the change in the manufacturing process? supply of price of leather belts artificial belts

options.A: decreases decreases
options.B: decreases increases
options.C: increases decreases
options.D: increases increases

questions.questionText: What is the likely price elasticity of supply of highly perishable goods and goods that have low stocks? highly goods that perishable have low goods stocks

options.A: elastic elastic
options.B: elastic inelastic
options.C: inelastic elastic
options.D: inelastic inelastic

questions.questionText: What is used to calculate the price elasticity of demand? change in price A change in quantity demanded change in quantity demanded B change in price percentage change in price C percentage change in quantity demanded percentage change in quantity demanded D percentage change in price
After a series of poor harvests, a government imposes an effective maximum price on cereals. What would be a consequence of this policy?

options.A: Both rich and poor people would satisfy their demands equally.
options.B: Illegal buying and selling through a black market would be prevented.
options.C: Rationing would be necessary to ensure a fair distribution of cereals.
options.D: The market would fail to clear leaving a surplus of cereals.

questions.questionText: What would be a transfer payment?

options.A: the payment made by a company to its shareholders out of its profits
options.B: the payment made for a legal document to transfer ownership of a house
options.C: the payment made to a retired person in the form of a pension
options.D: the payment made to a professional sports team for the transfer of a player

questions.questionText: The government redistributes income by raising the top rate of income tax and using the money raised to finance additional benefits to students and the unemployed. Under which conditions will total spending in the economy increase the most? income elasticity income elasticity of demand of top of demand of rate income students and the taxpayers unemployed

The diagram shows the supply of and demand for bricks. price of S bricks S P 2 P P D O quantity of bricks Which size of subsidy per unit is required to increase supply to S ?

options.A: OP B P P C P P D P P

questions.questionText: Why is national defence provided by the government?

options.A: In a free market it is excludable and rival in consumption.
options.B: In a free market it is non-excludable and non-rival in consumption.
options.C: The government has perfect information, so it can set the correct quantity required.
options.D: The private sector firm would charge a high price for its use as it is a necessity.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a rise in the general price level in a country is correct?

options.A: It is likely to create economic winners and losers in the country.
options.B: It is never acceptable to modern governments.
options.C: It means that no goods have fallen in price.
options.D: It must make the average citizen poorer.

questions.questionText: A country’s terms of trade changed from 100 to 95. What is most likely to have caused this change?

options.A: a depreciation of the country’s currency
options.B: a reduction in import tariffs
options.C: a rise in the price of exported goods
options.D: an improvement in the balance of trade

questions.questionText: A country replaces a floating exchange rate system with a managed floating exchange rate system. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Its central bank would have to intervene more frequently in the foreign exchange market.
options.B: Its central bank would need to hold fewer foreign currency reserves.
options.C: The value of its currency would be determined by its major trading partners.
options.D: The value of its currency would be determined by the value of the US dollar.

questions.questionText: What will be the immediate effect of a devaluation of an economy’s foreign exchange rate?

options.A: The price of imported goods in the domestic currency will fall.
options.B: The price of imported goods in the domestic currency will rise.
options.C: The price of imported goods in the foreign currency will fall.
options.D: The price of imported goods in the foreign currency will rise.

questions.questionText: A country has a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. What might help the country to reduce its deficit?

options.A: a decrease in its rate of income tax
options.B: a decrease in its tariffs
options.C: an increase in its level of employment
options.D: an increase in its subsidies to exporters

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of removing a tariff on imports of good X into country Y. S X domestic price of X (US$)
Which item should be recorded in the financial account of a country’s balance of payments?

options.A: foreign aid by China to assist in infrastructure projects in African countries
options.B: investments by Middle Eastern oil producing countries through the purchase of land and property assets in Europe
options.C: payments by the USA to other countries which house American military bases
options.D: profits and dividends paid by multinational companies based in Indonesia to shareholders in Asia

questions.questionText: The table shows a country’s consumer prices index (CPI) for March and April 2018. CPI March 2018 151.3 April 2018 148.6 Which statement correctly describes what happened between these two months?

options.A: There was a decrease in the annual rate of inflation.
options.B: There was a decrease in real interest rates.
options.C: There was an increase in the purchasing power of money.
options.D: There was an increase in the standard of living.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the rate of inflation over time in four countries. Which country has a rising real value of money over time? A inflation rate B C + time – D

The table shows the consumer prices index (CPI) for an economy expressed as an index number. year CPI 2016 100 2017 103 2018 101 2019 97 Which action is the government most likely to take to achieve price stability?

options.A: appreciate the exchange rate
options.B: decrease the budget deficit
options.C: increase the money supply
options.D: increase the rate of interest

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what is most likely to be reduced by falling labour productivity?

options.A: the balance of trade deficit
options.B: the internal value of money
options.C: the level of unemployment
options.D: the rate of domestic inflation
